keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's row 1450-1452 (29,911 km2, the same outline as the Visconti and Sforza duchies on either side) is mis-dated and too large. The page gives 'Established 1447; disestablished 1450', and says Pavia, Lodi and Piacenza defected or declared independence, Venice occupied Lodi and Piacenza and Sforza took Pavia. The corrected shape holds August 1447 to March 1450. The page gives no infobox area, so the factor-of-two check could not be made; subtracting the three provinces leaves about 23,000 km2.

ledger.note: Page silent on the date: Pavia declares itself independent and falls to Sforza. 'Sforza captured Pavia, and the Republic let him keep it with the title of Count.' The page dates neither the defection nor the capture, so 1447, the year of the proclamation, bridges the silence.

Page silent on the date: Lodi and Piacenza defect and Venice occupies them. 'Pavia, Lodi, and Piacenza defected or declared independence'; 'Venice occupied Lodi and Piacenza'; Piacenza was later sacked by Sforza (undated). The page gives no dates; 1447 bridges the silence.

region.text: the Milanese state as Filippo Maria Visconti left it on 13 August 1447, from which 'previously Milanese cities including Pavia, Lodi, and Piacenza defected or declared their independence' (losses in 1447)

ledger.note: 1447: Filippo Maria Visconti dies and Milan proclaims a republic. 'died on 13 August 1447'; the Bracceschi seized Milan that night and 'A republic was declared behind the Palace of the Commune' on the 14th (the page gives 'the 14th'; its sources date it to 14 August). Infobox: 'Established 1447'. (Reviewer eu-13-i: region changed from the outline minus Pavia, Lodi and Piacenza to the whole outline, so that the found event mirrors duchy-of-milan's 1447 loss of its 1440 outline and the two 1447 losses are not counted twice; the keyframe correction keeps the reduced shape.)

ledger.note: 1450: Francesco Sforza takes Milan and the republic ends. Gaspare da Vimercate and the Stampa family 'engineered a coup on 24 February' 1450; 'On 22 March 1450, he had himself declared capitano del popolo', and Duke of Milan by right of his wife. The Wars in Lombardy page has Sforza entering Milan 'in triumph' in May 1450. Infobox: 'disestablished 1450'.

wars.name: War of the Ambrosian Republic against Sforza and Venice
wars.outcome: The republic hired Sforza, who defected to Venice (treaty of 18 October 1448); Venice was beaten at Caravaggio in 1448 (the page: Attendolo attacked 'until 15 September'), the peace with Venice of 1449 was signed behind Sforza's back, the coup of 24 February 1450 let Sforza in and he was declared capitano del popolo on 22 March 1450; the Peace of Lodi in 1454 confirmed the House of Sforza.
wars.note: The Battle of Casalmaggiore and the Treaty of Rivoltella (1448) are not on the page.

certainty.note: The republic's real extent is unknown: the page names only Pavia, Lodi, Piacenza, Tortona and Crema as lost or contested, with no dates and no boundary.

notes: Pages opened: 2 of the 1-2 budgeted (the Wars in Lombardy page is shared with duchy-of-milan). Cliopatria's Ambrosian row (1450-1452) is mis-dated: the page gives August 1447 to March 1450, and Cliopatria's Duchy of Milan 1440-1449 and 1453-1462 rows share the same 29,911 km2 outline, so the republic's reduced extent (three provinces subtracted, about 23,000 km2) is a reading, not a surveyed boundary. Page disagreement: Sforza declared capitano del popolo on 22 March 1450 (Golden Ambrosian Republic) against 'entered Milan in triumph' in May 1450 (Wars in Lombardy); the end is recorded at March. Page silent: when Pavia, Lodi and Piacenza defected; Parma, Como, Novara and Alessandria; the Treaty of Rivoltella and Casalmaggiore; recognition of Sforza by other powers; Tortona (Colleoni) and Crema (Gonzaga offered it to Sforza in exchange for Tortona) were left out of the keyframe because the gazetteer lacks both names as places (Crema, Tortona: gazetteer_names_needed). The Ambrosian Republic's predecessor and successor are both duchy-of-milan; the Duchy dossier records the land as loss (1447) and gain (1450).
